items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: But when we made those films and things we made — ... Then we made some money with Ethel Waters

ctx.x: What were you coming home with, a week, in your pocket?

I’d say in the last band, you mean in the ‘39 band? Well it was better then, but not as ... what it should have been. We made several films and we would kind of get over, because we made “Hit Parade” of ‘43, with Dorothy Dandridge, and “Hellzapoppin” with Olson and Johnson I believe it was. Then we made some money with Ethel Waters, and was Lena Horne in there, I think she, no that was Cab in “Stormy Weather.” But when we made those films and things we made —
So you’d get royalties from that?
